user_message: What effect does consuming too much added sugar have on triglycerides and cholesterol levels?
assistant_response:
Great question! Consuming too much added sugar can have a significant negative impact on both your triglyceride and cholesterol levels.

## Effects on Triglycerides

**Elevated fasting triglycerides** are one of the most consistent effects of high sugar intake. According to the American Heart Association, diets high in added sugars—particularly sucrose (table sugar) and fructose—can raise plasma triglyceride levels. This effect is especially pronounced when:

- Added sugars make up a large portion of your daily calories (≥20% of energy)
- You have insulin resistance or glucose intolerance
- You consume sugar-sweetened beverages regularly

The World Health Organization and USDA Dietary Guidelines both identify limiting added sugars as one of the most important dietary strategies for managing elevated triglycerides.

## Effects on Cholesterol

High sugar intake also tends to **lower HDL cholesterol** (the "good" cholesterol that helps remove other forms of cholesterol from your bloodstream). This combination—high triglycerides paired with low HDL—is particularly concerning for cardiovascular health.

## Why This Happens

When you consume refined carbohydrates and added sugars, especially in excess, your liver converts them into triglycerides. The more added sugar you consume, the more triglycerides your body produces and releases into your bloodstream.

## Bottom Line

Limiting sugar-sweetened beverages and foods with added/refined sugars is one of the most evidence-based ways to help manage triglyceride levels and support healthier cholesterol ratios. If you're working on improving your triglycerides, reducing added sugar intake is an excellent place to start!
